source.text: Ἀπεκρίθησαν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Οὐ καλῶς λέγομεν ἡμεῖς ὅτι Σαμαρίτης εἶ σὺ καὶ δαιμόνιον ἔχεις;

records.literal_gloss: Answered the Jews and said to him, "Not well say we that a Samaritan are you and a demon you have?"

en.L: The Jews answered and said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Do we not say rightly that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are a Samaritan and have a demon?"
en.B: The Jews who were arguing with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} answered, "Are we not right to say that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are a Samaritan and have a demon?"
en.R: The Jews who were arguing with Jesus answered, "We are right about {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, are we not? You are a Samaritan, and a demon has driven {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} mad!"

es.L: Respondieron los judíos y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijeron: «¿No decimos bien nosotros que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} eres samaritano y tienes un demonio?».
es.B: Los judíos que discutían con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} respondieron: «¿No tenemos razón al decir que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} eres un samaritano y que tienes un demonio?».
es.R: Los judíos que discutían con Jesús {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} respondieron: «Tenemos razón acerca de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, ¿no es cierto? ¡Tú eres un samaritano, y un demonio {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} ha vuelto loco!».

fr.L: Les Juifs répondirent et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dirent : « Ne disons-nous pas à juste titre que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es un Samaritain et que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as un démon ? »
fr.B: Les Juifs qui débattaient avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} répliquèrent : « N’est-ce pas à bon droit que nous disons que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es un Samaritain et que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as un démon ? »
fr.R: Les Juifs qui débattaient avec Jésus ont répondu : « Nous avons raison à {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} sujet, n’est-ce pas ? Tu es un Samaritain, et un démon {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}a rendu fou ! »

sw.L: Wayahudi wakajibu, wakamwambia, "Je, hatusemi vema kwamba {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni Msamaria na una pepo?"
sw.B: Wayahudi waliokuwa wakibishana {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} wakajibu, "Je, hatuko sahihi kusema kwamba {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni Msamaria na una pepo?"
sw.R: Wayahudi waliokuwa wakibishana na Yesu wakajibu, "Tuko sahihi kuhusu wewe, sivyo? Wewe ni Msamaria, na pepo amekurukisha akili!"

vi.L: Những người Do Thái đáp và nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Chẳng phải chúng tôi nói đúng rằng ông là người Sa-ma-ri và có quỷ [trong người] sao?"
vi.B: Những người Do Thái đang tranh luận với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đáp: "Chúng tôi nói ông là người Sa-ma-ri và bị quỷ ám, chẳng phải là đúng sao?"
vi.R: Những người Do Thái đang tranh luận với Đức Giê-xu đáp: "Chúng tôi nói đúng về ông, phải không? Ông là người Sa-ma-ri, và ông bị quỷ ám nên điên rồi!"

ko.L: 유대인들이 대답하여 그분께 말했다. "네가 사마리아 사람이고 귀신이 들렸다고 우리가 말하는 것이 옳지 않으냐?"
ko.B: 그분과 논쟁하던 유대인들이 대답했다. "우리가 너를 사마리아 사람이라고, 귀신 들렸다고 하는 것이 옳지 않으냐?"
ko.R: 예수와 논쟁하던 유대인들이 대답했다. "우리 말이 맞지 않느냐? 너는 사마리아 사람이고, 귀신이 들려 미쳤다!"

pt.L: Os judeus responderam e {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} disseram: "Não dizemos nós com razão que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} és samaritano e tens um demônio?"
pt.B: Os judeus que discutiam com {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} responderam: "Não temos razão quando dizemos que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} és samaritano e tens um demônio?"
pt.R: Os judeus que discutiam com Jesus responderam: "Nós estamos certos sobre {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, não estamos? Tu és um samaritano, e um demônio {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} deixou louco!"

decisions.choice: the Jews: the hearers in the temple courts who were disputing with Jesus, the same group as in 8:31-47
alternatives: the Jewish people as a whole
decisions.reason: They answer what Jesus has just said to them (8:44-47). John introduced them in 8:31 as Jews who had believed him, and by 8:37 and 8:40 Jesus says they are seeking to kill him. The setting is the temple (8:20, 59). The word names this group of hearers, not the people as a whole: Jesus is himself a Jew (4:9, 22), and so are his disciples.

decisions.choice: Samaritan: an insult, branding him an outsider to Abraham's people
alternatives: a claim about where he was born
decisions.reason: They knew he came from Galilee (7:41, 52). Jews and Samaritans had long been divided (4:9), and Jews held that the Samaritans worshiped wrongly (4:20-22). To call a Jew a Samaritan was to say that he did not belong to Israel and taught falsely. It throws back his charge that they are not Abraham's true children (8:39-40).

decisions.choice: you have a demon: you are raving, in the grip of an evil spirit
decisions.reason: As in 7:20 and 10:20, the charge means that he is out of his mind. Here it also throws back his words of 8:44: he said that their father is the devil; they say that a demon is in him.

decisions.choice: Are we not right: a question that expects the answer yes
decisions.reason: The question with "not" expects agreement, and "we" is stressed: they claim they have been right about him all along (compare 7:20).

decisions.choice: the Jews who were arguing with him (B); the Jews who were arguing with Jesus (R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the hearers in this dispute (meaning decision m1), not the authorities alone and not the Jewish people as a whole. Balanced and Readable keep the word John wrote, as 8:31 does, and tie it to the people present, so that no reader takes it to mean every Jew.

decisions.choice: a demon has driven you mad (R)
alternatives: you are out of your mind (as 7:20)
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the insult (meaning decision m3), as 7:20 does, but keeps the demon, because Jesus answers that very word in verse 49 and it throws back his words about the devil (8:44).

decisions.choice: los judíos (L); los judíos que discutían con él / que estaban allí (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the hearers in this dispute (meaning decision m1), not the authorities alone and not the Jewish people as a whole, so no level says "dirigentes".

decisions.choice: un demonio te ha vuelto loco
decisions.reason: As in English: gives the sense of the insult but keeps the demon, because Jesus answers that charge (meaning decision m3). Every plural "you" in this passage is the ustedes / vosotros setting.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (B) and the passé composé (R); Literal keeps John's tenses (passé simple for his past tenses, the present where he uses it); speech in the passé composé at every level
decisions.reason: The French brief for this passage (8:48-59), as in 8:31-47: the passé simple is the tense of written narrative and suits a public reading, and Readable uses the passé composé, the past tense young readers know. Inside speech every level uses the passé composé ("Abraham est mort", "tu as vu").

decisions.choice: les Juifs (L); les Juifs qui débattaient avec lui (B); les Juifs qui débattaient avec Jésus (R); les Juifs qui étaient là (8:52, 57)
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for John: Literal keeps the word John wrote. Here it names the hearers in this dispute, not the authorities alone and not the whole people (meaning decision m1), so Balanced and Readable keep "les Juifs" and say which Jews, as the English does; "les chefs juifs" would narrow it wrongly.

decisions.choice: the opponents call Jesus "ông" and themselves "chúng tôi"; Jesus calls them "các người"
decisions.reason: The forms of address kept through 8:31-59. "Ông" is polite but distant, fitting hearers who reject his claims; "Thầy" would grant him the standing they deny.

decisions.choice: "có quỷ [trong người]" (L); "bị quỷ ám" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese cannot say "have a demon" without saying where; Balanced and Readable use the ordinary idiom for demon possession.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean
alternatives: capitalised pronoun alternatives, as in the English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change. Respect for Jesus and God is carried at every level by the subject honorific -si-, by "께서" and by "그분".

decisions.choice: The hearers now speak to Jesus in the plain style without honorifics ("너", -느냐) through 8:59
alternatives: the formal style (합쇼체) they used in 8:33-41
decisions.reason: The style guide allows open opponents to speak to Jesus without honorifics where the scene is hostile. Here they call him a Samaritan and demon-possessed, and in 8:59 they take up stones; the drop from the formal speech of 8:33-41 marks the turn. The narrator keeps the honorific for Jesus (그분께).

decisions.choice: tu, from his opponents
decisions.reason: Jesus's opponents speak to him with "tu", as everyone who addresses him does (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 4); the insult is in their words, not in the form of address. "Você" would make this exchange the only one in the Gospel where Jesus is addressed as an equal.

source.text: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς· Ἐγὼ δαιμόνιον οὐκ ἔχω, ἀλλὰ τιμῶ τὸν πατέρα μου, καὶ ὑμεῖς ἀτιμάζετέ με.

records.literal_gloss: Answered Jesus, "I a demon not have, but I honor the Father of me, and you dishonor me.

en.L: Jesus answered, "I do not have a demon, but I honor {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father, and you dishonor {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: Jesus answered, "I do not have a demon. Rather, I honor {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father, and you dishonor {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: Jesus answered, "I do not have a demon. I give honor to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father, and you are insulting {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: Respondió Jesús: «Yo no tengo un demonio, sino que honro a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Padre, y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:deshonran|deshonráis}}.
es.B: Jesús respondió: «Yo no tengo un demonio. Al contrario, honro a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Padre, y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:deshonran|deshonráis}}.
es.R: Jesús respondió: «Yo no tengo un demonio. Yo honro a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Padre, y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:están insultando|estáis insultando}}.

fr.L: Jésus répondit : « Moi, je n’ai pas de démon, mais j’honore {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père, et vous, vous {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} déshonorez.
fr.B: Jésus répondit : « Je n’ai pas de démon. Au contraire, j’honore {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père, et vous, vous {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} déshonorez.
fr.R: Jésus a répondu : « Je n’ai pas de démon. Moi, je rends honneur à {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père, et vous, vous {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}insultez.

sw.L: Yesu akajibu, "Mimi sina pepo, bali namheshimu Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, nanyi mnanivunjia heshima.
sw.B: Yesu akajibu, "Sina pepo. Badala yake namheshimu Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, nanyi mnanidharau.
sw.R: Yesu akajibu, "Sina pepo. Nampa heshima Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, nanyi mnanitukana.

vi.L: Đức Giê-xu đáp: "Ta không có quỷ [trong người], nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} tôn kính Cha của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, còn các người làm nhục {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu đáp: "Ta không bị quỷ ám. Trái lại, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} tôn kính Cha của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, còn các người thì sỉ nhục {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu đáp: "Ta không bị quỷ ám. Ta tôn kính Cha của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, còn các người thì xúc phạm {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.

ko.L: 예수께서 대답하셨다. "나는 귀신 들린 것이 아니라 내 아버지를 공경한다. 그런데 너희는 나를 업신여긴다.
ko.B: 예수께서 대답하셨다. "나는 귀신 들리지 않았다. 오히려 나는 내 아버지를 공경하는데, 너희는 나를 모욕한다.
ko.R: 예수께서 대답하셨다. "나는 귀신 들리지 않았다. 나는 내 아버지를 높이고 있는데, 너희는 나를 모욕하고 있다.

pt.L: Jesus respondeu: "Eu não tenho demônio, mas honro o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} Pai, e vocês {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} desonram.
pt.B: Jesus respondeu: "Eu não tenho demônio. Pelo contrário, honro o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} Pai, e vocês {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} desonram.
pt.R: Jesus respondeu: "Eu não tenho demônio nenhum. Eu dou honra ao {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} Pai, e vocês estão {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} insultando.

decisions.choice: I do not have a demon: he answers the second charge only
decisions.reason: Jesus does not trouble to deny that he is a Samaritan. The charge that matters is that his words come from an evil power. The stressed "I" sets him against his accusers, and the stressed "you" at the end answers it.

decisions.choice: honor and dishonor: giving or refusing the respect a person is due
decisions.reason: Honor was a person's public standing, and an insult took it away. Jesus speaks what the Father has taught him and does what pleases him (8:28-29), so in speaking he honors the Father; their insult falls on the one who sent him as well (5:23).

decisions.choice: Rather
decisions.reason: Balanced makes the denial its own sentence and lets "Rather" carry the contrast of the Greek "but".

decisions.choice: give honor to, are insulting (R)
decisions.reason: Readable uses everyday words for the pair (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: me están insultando (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: everyday words for the pair (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} for Jesus speaking of himself, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} for him and for the Father; plain "Ta" at the start of a sentence; "Cha của Ta" rather than "Cha Ta"
decisions.reason: Only the capital letter changes with the setting. "Của" keeps the possessive from being read as the colloquial "cha ta" (our father) when the setting shows lowercase.

source.text: ἐγὼ δὲ οὐ ζητῶ τὴν δόξαν μου· ἔστιν ὁ ζητῶν καὶ κρίνων.

records.literal_gloss: I but not seek the glory of me; is the [one] seeking and judging.

en.L: But I do not seek {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} glory; there is one who seeks [it] and judges.
en.B: But I do not seek {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own glory. There is one who seeks it, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} judges.
en.R: I am not trying to get glory for {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}. But there is one who wants glory for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the judge.

es.L: Pero yo no busco {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} gloria; hay quien [la] busca y juzga.
es.B: Pero yo no busco {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} propia gloria. Hay uno que la busca, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} juzga.
es.R: Yo no estoy buscando gloria para {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. Pero hay uno que quiere gloria para {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es el juez.

fr.L: Mais {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je ne cherche pas {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} gloire ; il y a quelqu’un qui [la] cherche et qui juge.
fr.B: Mais je ne cherche pas {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} propre gloire. Il y en a un qui la cherche, et c’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui juge.
fr.R: Je n’essaie pas d’obtenir de la gloire pour {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. Mais il y a quelqu’un qui veut {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} donner de la gloire, et c’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} le juge.

sw.L: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} siutafuti utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}; yupo anayeutafuta [huo] na kuhukumu.
sw.B: Lakini siutafuti utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}. Yupo anayeutafuta, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} ndiye anayehukumu.
sw.R: Sijaribu kujipatia utukufu {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}. Lakini yupo anayetaka nipate utukufu, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} ndiye mwamuzi.

vi.L: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không tìm vinh quang của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; có Đấng tìm [vinh quang ấy] và xét xử.
vi.B: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không tìm vinh quang cho riêng mình. Có một Đấng tìm vinh quang ấy, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} xét xử.
vi.R: Ta không tìm vinh quang cho chính mình. Nhưng có một Đấng muốn tôn vinh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là Đấng xét xử.

ko.L: 그러나 나는 내 영광을 구하지 않는다. [그것을] 구하시고 심판하시는 분이 계시다.
ko.B: 그러나 나는 내 영광을 구하지 않는다. 그 영광을 구하시는 분이 계시고, 그분이 심판하신다.
ko.R: 나는 나 자신의 영광을 얻으려고 하지 않는다. 그러나 나에게 영광을 주시려는 분이 계시고, 그분이 심판하는 분이시다.

pt.L: Mas eu não busco a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} glória; há quem [a] busque e julgue.
pt.B: Mas eu não busco a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} própria glória. Há alguém que a busca, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} julga.
pt.R: Eu não estou procurando glória para {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} mesmo. Mas existe alguém que quer glória para {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} é o juiz.

decisions.choice: my glory: honor, a good name
decisions.reason: Here glory is the honor a person seeks or receives, as in 5:41-44 and 7:18: one who seeks his own glory speaks on his own authority. It carries on the talk of honor in verse 49.

decisions.choice: the one who seeks and judges: the Father, who upholds the Son's honor and decides between him and his accusers
decisions.reason: Verse 54 names him: it is the Father who glorifies the Son. "Judges" here means that he will decide the case between Jesus and those who dishonor him. In 5:22 the Father has given all judging to the Son; here the Father is the one who vindicates the Son (compare 8:16, 29).

decisions.choice: seeks: the object is understood from the first half
decisions.reason: The Greek gives no object for "seeks"; it is "my glory" carried over from the first half.

decisions.choice: [it] (L); it, he judges (B); wants glory for me, he is the judge (R)
decisions.reason: English needs the object that the Greek leaves understood (meaning decision m3). Readable says plainly whose glory is meant, without naming the Father, which Jesus leaves to verse 54.

decisions.choice: [la] (L); la (B); quiere gloria para mí (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: supplies the object the Greek leaves understood (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: c’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui juge (B); c’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} le juge (R)
decisions.reason: The one who seeks Jesus's glory is the Father (meaning decision m2), so the pronoun French needs here takes the deity_pronoun setting, as the English "he" does. Literal has no pronoun, as the Greek.

decisions.choice: "Đấng" for "the one who seeks"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese must choose a classifier for the person; "Đấng" is the one used of God, whom Jesus means, as the meaning decision says.

decisions.choice: Jesus speaks of the Father with the honorific (구하시고, 계시다)
alternatives: no honorific, like Jesus's words about himself
decisions.reason: In Korean a speaker honours God in the third person while using plain forms of himself; this keeps "the one who seeks and judges" clearly the Father.

source.text: ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐάν τις τὸν ἐμὸν λόγον τηρήσῃ, θάνατον οὐ μὴ θεωρήσῃ εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα.

records.literal_gloss: Truly truly I say to you, if anyone the my word keeps, death not not will see into the age."

en.L: Truly, truly I say to you, if anyone keeps {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word, {{gender:they|he}} will never see death."
en.B: Truly, truly, I tell you, if anyone keeps {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word, {{gender:they|he}} will never see death."
en.R: I tell you the truth: anyone who holds on to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} teaching and obeys it will never see death."

es.L: En verdad, en verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que si alguien guarda {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} palabra, jamás verá la muerte».
es.B: En verdad, en verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que, si alguien guarda {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} palabra, nunca verá la muerte».
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad: quien se aferre a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} enseñanza y la obedezca nunca verá la muerte».

fr.L: En vérité, en vérité, je vous le dis : si quelqu’un garde {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} parole, il ne verra jamais la mort. »
fr.B: En vérité, en vérité, je vous le dis : si quelqu’un garde {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} parole, jamais il ne verra la mort. »
fr.R: Je vous le dis, c’est la vérité : celui qui reste attaché à {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} enseignement et le met en pratique ne verra jamais la mort. »

pt.L: Em verdade, em verdade eu lhes digo: se alguém guardar a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} palavra, jamais verá a morte, para sempre."
pt.B: Em verdade, em verdade eu lhes digo: se alguém guardar a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} palavra, nunca verá a morte."
pt.R: Eu garanto a vocês: quem se apegar ao {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} ensino e viver de acordo com ele nunca vai ver a morte."

decisions.choice: keeps my word: holds to his teaching and obeys it
decisions.reason: To keep a word is to hold on to it and live by it (14:23; 15:20; 17:6). It takes up 8:31, "if you remain in my word". "Word" is his whole message, which they cannot bear to hear (8:37, 43).

decisions.choice: see death: experience death
decisions.reason: To "see death" is a Hebrew way of saying to die (Psalm 89:49; Luke 2:26; Hebrews 11:5). Jesus speaks of death as the end of life with God: whoever believes has passed from death to life (5:24), and will live even though he dies (11:25-26). He does not promise escape from bodily dying, but his hearers take it so (verse 52).

decisions.choice: never: the strongest denial, for all time
decisions.reason: Two negatives stand together, the strongest way of denying that something will happen, and "to the age" adds "for all time" (as in 10:28 and 11:26).

decisions.choice: Truly, truly I say to you (L); Truly, truly, I tell you (B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering for John (see 1:51), recorded once in this passage; it covers 8:58 as well.

decisions.choice: if anyone ..., they (default) or he (traditional)
decisions.reason: "Anyone" means any person, man or woman; the gender setting gives the traditional "he". Readable says "anyone who" and needs no pronoun.

decisions.choice: holds on to my teaching and obeys it
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what keeping his word means (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: En verdad, en verdad les digo (L, B); Les digo la verdad (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide Spanish rendering, recorded once in this passage; it covers 8:58.

decisions.choice: no gender setting
decisions.reason: "Si alguien ... verá" needs no pronoun in Spanish, so no setting is needed, here or in 8:52.

decisions.choice: En vérité, en vérité, je vous le dis (L, B); Je vous le dis, c’est la vérité (R)
alternatives: Amen, amen, je vous le dis
Oui, vraiment, je vous le dis
decisions.reason: The book-wide French rendering for John, recorded once in this passage; it covers 8:58 as well. Readable puts the pledge in plain words.

decisions.choice: no gender setting: "si quelqu’un ..., il" (L, B); "celui qui" (R)
decisions.reason: English puts "they/he" under the gender setting. In French "il" taking up the indefinite "quelqu’un" is the grammatical agreement and reads as "anyone", as in 7:17; a doubled "il ou elle" would be heavy. Readable uses "celui qui", the usual general form.

decisions.choice: "Thật vậy, thật vậy, Ta nói với các người" (L, B); "Ta nói thật với các người" (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide form of "Truly, truly", here and in 8:58.

decisions.choice: "ai ... người ấy", with no gender span
alternatives: a gender setting span, as in the English
decisions.reason: "Người ấy" (that person) is already inclusive, so Vietnamese has nothing for the gender setting to change.

decisions.choice: "진실로 진실로 너희에게 말한다" (L, B); "내가 분명히 말한다" (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide Korean choice for amen amen: modern plain-style ending instead of the archaic "이르노니"; Readable says the same solemn assurance in everyday words.

decisions.choice: No gender span: "누구든지" with no pronoun
decisions.reason: Korean "누구든지" (anyone) needs no following pronoun and is already inclusive, so the gender setting has nothing to change here.

decisions.choice: Em verdade, em verdade eu lhes digo (L, B); Eu garanto a vocês (R)
decisions.reason: John's doubled formula as docs/portuguese-style.md, section 6, gives it; recorded once in this passage, it covers 8:58 as well. Readable says "Eu garanto a vocês", as the English Readable says "I tell you the truth".

decisions.choice: se alguém ..., with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The English needs a setting for the pronoun after "anyone". Portuguese leaves the subject of "verá" unexpressed, so "alguém" covers men and women without a pronoun and no setting is needed (also in verse 52).

decisions.choice: jamais verá a morte, para sempre
alternatives: não verá a morte para sempre
decisions.reason: Literal shows both the double negative and "to the age" (meaning decision m3); "não ... para sempre" alone could be read as "will not see death forever", that is, only for a time.

decisions.choice: the Jews: the same hearers as in verse 48
alternatives: the Jewish people as a whole
decisions.reason: The dispute goes on with the same people who were arguing with Jesus in the temple courts (8:31-48). Not the people as a whole: Jesus and his disciples are Jews.

decisions.choice: now we know: his last words have settled it for them
decisions.reason: The perfect tense means "we have come to know, and are sure". "Now" points to what he has just said (verse 51): to them the claim proves the charge of verse 48.

decisions.choice: the Jews there (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the hearers in this dispute (meaning decision m1), not the authorities alone and not the Jewish people as a whole. Balanced and Readable keep the word John wrote, as 8:31 does, and tie it to the people present, so that no reader takes it to mean every Jew.

decisions.choice: a demon has driven you mad
decisions.reason: As in verse 48 (rendering decision r-en-2 there).

decisions.choice: los judíos (L); los judíos que discutían con él / que estaban allí (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the hearers in this dispute (meaning decision m1), not the authorities alone and not the Jewish people as a whole, so no level says "dirigentes".

records.literal_gloss: Abraham died and the prophets, and you say, 'If anyone the word of me keeps, not not will he taste of death into the age';

pt.L: Abraão morreu, e os profetas, e {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} dizes: 'Se alguém guardar a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} palavra, jamais provará a morte, para sempre.'
pt.B: Abraão morreu, e os profetas também, e mesmo assim {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} dizes: 'Se alguém guardar a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} palavra, nunca provará a morte.'
pt.R: Abraão morreu, e os profetas também morreram. Mas {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} dizes que quem obedecer ao {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} ensino nunca vai morrer.

decisions.choice: taste death: experience death, die
decisions.reason: "Taste death" is another way of saying to die (Mark 9:1; Hebrews 2:9). In quoting Jesus they change "see" to "taste", but the sense is the same. The quotation is otherwise close to his words of verse 51.

decisions.choice: Abraham died: they take his words of bodily death
alternatives: they deny any life after death
decisions.reason: As often in John, the hearers take Jesus's words at the bodily level (3:4; 4:11; 6:52). Abraham and the prophets were the greatest of God's servants, and they died; how can this man's word do what theirs could not? Jesus spoke of the death that cuts a person off from God (verse 51, meaning decision m2 there).

decisions.choice: if anyone ..., they (default) or he (traditional)
decisions.reason: As in verse 51.

decisions.choice: you say that anyone who obeys your teaching will never die
alternatives: a direct quotation, as in Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: Readable reports the words instead of quoting them and gives the plain sense of "taste death" (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: probará la muerte
decisions.reason: Spanish "probar la muerte" keeps their change from "ver" to "probar" (meaning decision m1); Readable says "morirá".

decisions.choice: goûter la mort
decisions.reason: "Goûter la mort" is understood in French as "to die" and keeps the change from "see" (verse 51) to "taste" that the hearers make (meaning decision m1). Readable says "ne mourra jamais", as the English does. As in verse 51, "il" after "quelqu’un" needs no gender setting.

decisions.choice: Jesus's own "Ta" kept inside their quotation of him
decisions.reason: They quote his words as he said them; in the indirect speech of Readable it becomes "ông".

decisions.choice: "예언자" for prophētēs
decisions.reason: As through the book (docs/korean-style.md): "예언자" is the current word that new readers understand; "선지자" is the established older Protestant term, and a reviewer may prefer it for the whole book.

decisions.choice: No gender span: "누구든지" with no pronoun
decisions.reason: Korean "누구든지" (anyone) needs no following pronoun and is already inclusive, so the gender setting has nothing to change here.

ko.L: 설마 네가 죽은 우리 아버지 아브라함보다 더 크냐?
ko.B: 설마 네가 우리 아버지 아브라함보다 더 크다는 말이냐? 그는 죽었다.
ko.R: 네가 우리 아버지 아브라함보다 더 위대하다고 생각하느냐? 그도 죽었다.

pt.L: Acaso {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} és maior que o nosso pai Abraão, que morreu?
pt.B: Por acaso {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} és maior que o nosso pai Abraão? Ele morreu.
pt.R: Tu achas que és maior que o nosso pai Abraão? Ele morreu.

decisions.choice: a question expecting the answer no
decisions.reason: The question is framed to expect "no". John's readers know the answer is yes; the Samaritan woman asked the same of Jacob (4:12).

decisions.choice: who died: great as he was, he died
decisions.reason: The relative pronoun has the sense "one who, for all his greatness, died". Death is their whole point: if Abraham could not escape it, no one can promise others they will.

decisions.choice: our father Abraham: the ancestor of Israel
decisions.reason: Abraham was the father of the nation, and their descent from him was their boast (8:33, 39). The chapter has turned on who their father truly is (8:38-44).

decisions.choice: Do you think you are greater
alternatives: Surely you are not greater (Literal, Balanced)
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the expected answer "no" (meaning decision m1) in words young readers know. It keeps "father", not "ancestor" as in 4:12, because the talk of fathers runs through this chapter.

decisions.choice: ¿Crees que tú eres más grande ...?
decisions.reason: As in English: keeps the expected answer "no" (meaning decision m1). "Él" here is Abraham and has no setting.

decisions.choice: Serais-tu ... ? (L); Tout de même, tu n’es pas ... ? (B)
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer no (meaning decision m1). French marks that with the conditional of doubt (Literal) or with "tout de même pas" (Balanced); a plain "Es-tu ... ?" would be an open question. Readable uses "tu te crois", as the English says "do you think".

decisions.choice: Acaso (L); Por acaso (B)
decisions.reason: Portuguese marks a question that expects "no" with "acaso" / "por acaso" (meaning decision m1), where English says "Surely ... not".

decisions.choice: make yourself: claim to be, without right
alternatives: what are you trying to become
decisions.reason: They accuse him of claiming a rank that is not his, as in 5:18 ("making himself equal to God"), 10:33 and 19:7. John's irony: Jesus makes himself nothing; it is the Father who glorifies him (verse 54).

decisions.choice: and the prophets died: the point of verse 52 repeated
decisions.reason: They repeat the prophets' death to drive home the challenge. The question that follows is a rebuke, not a request for information.

decisions.choice: Who do you think you are (B); Who do you claim to be (R)
alternatives: Whom do you make yourself [to be] (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the everyday form of the challenge; Readable says plainly what they accuse him of (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: ¿Quién te crees que eres? (B); ¿Quién dices que eres? (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: the everyday form of the challenge (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: Pour qui te fais-tu passer ?
decisions.reason: The Greek is "whom do you make yourself?"; French "se faire passer pour" (to pass oneself off as) keeps the verb "faire" and the reflexive, and says what they accuse him of (meaning decision m1). Balanced uses the everyday challenge "Pour qui te prends-tu ?".

records.literal_gloss: Answered Jesus, "If I glorify myself, the glory of me nothing is; is the Father of me the [one] glorifying me, whom you say that 'God of us he is,' \v 55 and not you have known him, I but know him; and if I say that not I know him, I will be like to you a liar; but I know him and the word of him I keep.

It is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father who glorifies {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, of whom you say, 'He is our God.' \v 55 And you have not known {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, but I know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. And if I were to say that I do not know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, I would be a liar like you. But I know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word.

decisions.choice: glorify: honor that comes from God, not honor a person claims
decisions.reason: Glory a person gives himself is empty (5:41-44; 7:18). The Father glorifies the Son: in his signs (11:4), and above all in his "hour", his death and return to the Father (12:23; 13:31-32; 17:1, 5). It answers their question "Who do you make yourself out to be?" (verse 53).

decisions.choice: our God (SBLGNT): their own words, quoted
alternatives: "your God" (some manuscripts): Jesus's words about them
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts read "your God", so that Jesus says in his own words whom they call God. The SBLGNT reads "our God", and the word "that" then introduces their own words. The sense is the same either way. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: have known, know: two verbs, one meaning
decisions.reason: John uses both verbs for knowing God (7:28-29; 17:3, 25), and the change here is most likely for variety. The perfect "you have not known" says they have never come to know him; Jesus knows him as the one who comes from him (7:29).

decisions.choice: if I were to say ... I would be: a supposition he rejects
decisions.reason: To deny that he knows the Father would make him a liar, like those who claim God as Father but do not know him. It recalls 8:44, where the devil is a liar and the father of lies.

decisions.choice: keep his word: obey what the Father says
decisions.reason: Jesus does himself what he asks of others (verse 51): he keeps the Father's word, as his disciples are to keep his (15:10).

decisions.choice: give glory to, gives me glory; obey what he says (R)
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the key term as "glory" in a phrase young readers know, and spells out "keep his word" (meaning decision m5).

decisions.choice: were to say ... would be (L); said ... would be (B, R)
alternatives: if I say ... I will be
decisions.reason: English marks the supposition as unreal (meaning decision m4); the Greek future "I will be" is put as "I would be".

decisions.choice: me da gloria; obedezco lo que él dice (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: keeps "gloria" and spells out "guardar su palabra" (meaning decisions m1, m5).

decisions.choice: si dijera ... sería
decisions.reason: As in English: marks the supposition as unreal (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}}, {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}, {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} for the Father; {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} for Jesus
decisions.reason: Every pronoun for the Father and for Jesus takes the deity_pronoun setting, as in English; French needs object pronouns before the verb ("je le connais"), each with its own span. "Il" at the start of the quoted sentence is written plainly with its capital.

decisions.choice: "영광스럽게 하다" (L, B); "영광을 돌리다 / 영광을 주시다" (R)
decisions.reason: "영광스럽게 하다" is the key term for doxazō. Readable keeps the noun "영광" in everyday verbs, as the English Readable says "give glory to".

decisions.choice: se eu dissesse ... seria
decisions.reason: As the English, the Greek future is put as an unreal supposition (meaning decision m4); Portuguese does this with the imperfect subjunctive and the conditional.

decisions.choice: rejoiced that he might see: joy looking ahead to what he would see
decisions.reason: The verb of great joy is followed by "that he might see", which points to something still ahead of him. The second half says that he did see it.

decisions.choice: my day: the time of Jesus's coming and work
alternatives: the day of judgment at the end
only the day of his death and rising
decisions.reason: The prophets spoke of "the day of the Lord"; Jesus speaks of "my day", the time when he would come and do the Father's work. The phrase is not defined further, and it may take in his whole coming.

decisions.choice: he saw it: Abraham saw the day ahead, in God's promise
alternatives: he saw it from beyond death, in Jesus's own lifetime
he saw it in a vision
decisions.reason: Jesus does not say when or how Abraham saw it. Scripture gives Abraham the promise that all nations would be blessed through his offspring (Genesis 12:3; 22:18), and at the binding of Isaac he said that God would provide (Genesis 22:8, 14). His laughter at the promise of a son (Genesis 17:17) was read by some ancient Jewish interpreters as joy. Hebrews 11:13 says that the fathers saw what was promised from far off and welcomed it. Any of these may lie behind the saying; marked uncertain.

decisions.choice: your father: their ancestor by descent
decisions.reason: Jesus grants that they are Abraham's descendants (8:37), though he has denied that they act as his children (8:39-40). Abraham welcomed the day they now reject.

decisions.choice: was full of joy at the hope of seeing ... it made him glad
alternatives: rejoiced that he might see ... was glad (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the two verbs of joy in natural English and shows that the first looks ahead (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: the day when I would come
decisions.reason: Readable says what "my day" refers to (meaning decision m2). It names his coming in general, without choosing among the views of when Abraham saw it.

decisions.choice: el padre de ustedes / vuestro padre
decisions.reason: "Su padre" could be read as "his father"; the span keeps the owner plain.

decisions.choice: el día en que yo vendría
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable says what "my day" refers to (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: a exulté dans l’attente de voir (L); a débordé de joie dans l’espérance de voir (B)
alternatives: a tressailli de joie de ce qu’il verrait
decisions.reason: The first verb is one of great joy that looks ahead to what he would see (meaning decision m1); "dans l’attente" and "dans l’espérance" say that it was still to come. The second verb of joy is plainer: "s’est réjoui", "heureux".

decisions.choice: exultou [na expectativa de] ver
decisions.reason: Portuguese cannot join "exultar" to "that he might see" as the Greek does; the bracket shows the words Literal adds so that the joy looks ahead (meaning decision m1). "Por ver" would say he rejoiced because he had seen.

pt.L: Então os judeus {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} disseram: "Ainda não tens cinquenta anos, e {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} viste Abraão?"

decisions.choice: the Jews: the same hearers as in verses 48 and 52
alternatives: the Jewish people as a whole
decisions.reason: The same people who were arguing with Jesus in the temple courts. Not the people as a whole: Jesus and his disciples are Jews.

decisions.choice: not yet fifty: a round figure for a man not yet old
alternatives: a guess at his actual age
decisions.reason: They are not stating his age but saying he is far too young to have known Abraham. Fifty marked full maturity: Levites served until that age (Numbers 4:3; 8:24-25). Luke 3:23 says Jesus was about thirty when he began his work.

decisions.choice: and you have seen Abraham? (SBLGNT)
alternatives: "and has Abraham seen you?" (a few manuscripts, among them P75 and the first hand of Codex Sinaiticus)
decisions.reason: A few manuscripts, some of them early, have Abraham as the one who sees, which is closer to what Jesus said in verse 56. The SBLGNT reading has the hearers turn his words around: he had said that Abraham saw his day. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the Jews there (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the hearers in this dispute (meaning decision m1), not the authorities alone and not the Jewish people as a whole. Balanced and Readable keep the word John wrote, as 8:31 does, and tie it to the people present, so that no reader takes it to mean every Jew.

decisions.choice: two sentences, with "How could you have seen"
alternatives: and you have seen Abraham? (Literal, Balanced)
decisions.reason: Readable makes the scorn of the question plain.

decisions.choice: los judíos (L); los judíos que discutían con él / que estaban allí (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the hearers in this dispute (meaning decision m1), not the authorities alone and not the Jewish people as a whole, so no level says "dirigentes".

decisions.choice: Tu n’as pas encore cinquante ans
alternatives: Tu n’as pas encore cinquante ans [d’âge]
decisions.reason: French gives age with "avoir" and "ans", as the Greek does ("fifty years you do not yet have"), so Literal needs no bracket where the English adds "[old]".

vi.B: Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Thật vậy, thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các người, trước khi có Áp-ra-ham, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} Hằng Hữu."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Ta nói thật với các người: trước khi Áp-ra-ham được sinh ra, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} Hằng Hữu."

ko.L: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "진실로 진실로 너희에게 말한다. 아브라함이 생겨나기 전에 나는 있다."
ko.B: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "진실로 진실로 너희에게 말한다. 아브라함이 있기 전에 나는 있다."
ko.R: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "내가 분명히 말한다. 아브라함이 태어나기도 전에 나는 있다."

pt.L: Jesus lhes disse: "Em verdade, em verdade eu lhes digo: antes de Abraão vir a existir, Eu sou."
pt.B: Jesus lhes disse: "Em verdade, em verdade eu lhes digo: antes que Abraão existisse, Eu sou."
pt.R: Jesus lhes disse: "Eu garanto a vocês: antes mesmo de Abraão nascer, Eu sou."

decisions.choice: came to be / I am: a beginning set against being without beginning
alternatives: only that Jesus existed earlier than Abraham
decisions.reason: For Abraham Jesus uses a verb of coming into being; for himself he does not say "I was" but the present "I am". The same contrast opens the Gospel: the Word "was" in the beginning, while all things "came to be" through him (1:1-3).

decisions.choice: I am: the words with which God names himself
alternatives: only a claim to have lived before Abraham
decisions.reason: The words stand with no predicate. God names himself "I am" (Exodus 3:14), and in the Greek of Isaiah he says "I am" of himself (Isaiah 41:4; 43:10-13). In 6:20 the plain sense "it is I" was uppermost, and in 8:24 and 8:28 the words were veiled; here no plain sense fits. The hearers' answer in verse 59 shows how they understood him: the law's penalty for blasphemy was stoning (Leviticus 24:16; compare 10:31-33). A footnote notes the echo.

decisions.choice: I am (every level)
decisions.reason: The book's terms keep "before Abraham was, I am" at every level, so that the present tense and the echo of God's name (meaning decisions m1 and m2) stay visible. English can bear the change of tense; smoothing it would hide what the hearers reacted to.

decisions.choice: came to be (L); was (B); was even born (R)
decisions.reason: Literal shows the verb of coming into being; Balanced keeps the book's wording "before Abraham was"; Readable says it plainly. Only the first half changes; every level ends with "I am".

decisions.choice: yo soy at every level
decisions.reason: The book's terms keep "before Abraham was, I am" at every level, so the present tense and the echo of God's name stay (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: llegara a ser (L); existiera (B); naciera (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Literal shows the verb of coming into being. Balanced says "existiera" rather than "fuera", which could also mean "went".

decisions.choice: avant qu’Abraham vienne à l’existence (L), existe (B), soit né (R) ... je suis (every level)
decisions.reason: The book's choice keeps the bare "je suis" at every level, so that the present tense and the echo of God's name stay visible (meaning decisions m1 and m2). The first half shows Abraham's coming into being: Literal with the verb of becoming, Balanced with "exister", Readable with "naître". "Avant qu’Abraham fût" is the traditional wording, but its imperfect subjunctive is now only literary.

decisions.choice: "Ta Hằng Hữu" (I ever exist) at every level
decisions.reason: The guide keeps "I am" in the present at every level so that the echo of God's name stays. Vietnamese "là" cannot end a sentence, so a bare "Ta là" reads as cut off; "hằng hữu" (ever existing) keeps the present tense and echoes God's name in Exodus 3:14 ("Đấng Hằng Hữu"), the form used for "I am" in 8:24, 8:28 and 13:19. "Ta đã có" (I already existed) would lose both.

decisions.choice: "나는 있다" (present tense) at every level
decisions.reason: Korean grammar expects a past tense after "before Abraham"; the present "있다" is kept on purpose so that the contrast between Abraham's beginning and Jesus's timeless being, and the echo of God's "I am", stay visible as the meaning decisions describe. The archaic "-느니라" is avoided.

decisions.choice: Eu sou (every level), with a capital
decisions.reason: As the book's terms: the present tense stays at every level, so that the contrast with Abraham's coming to be and the echo of God's name (meaning decisions m1 and m2) remain visible; Portuguese bears the clash of tenses as English does. English "I" is always written with a capital; Portuguese "eu" is not, so the capital here marks the words as a name, as the English reader sees "I am" standing alone. "Eu era" or "eu já existia" would be smoother and lose the echo.

source.text: ἦραν οὖν λίθους ἵνα βάλωσιν ἐπ’ αὐτόν· Ἰησοῦς δὲ ἐκρύβη καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἐκ τοῦ ἱεροῦ.

es.R: Entonces agarraron piedras para tirárselas. Pero Jesús se escondió y salió del patio del templo.

fr.B: Alors ils ramassèrent des pierres pour les jeter sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, mais Jésus se cacha et sortit de la cour du temple.

vi.B: Nghe vậy, họ nhặt đá để ném {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, nhưng Đức Giê-xu ẩn mình và ra khỏi sân đền thờ.

ko.L: 그러자 그들이 돌을 들어 그분을 향해 던지려고 했다. 그러나 예수께서는 몸을 숨기시고 성전에서 나가셨다.
ko.B: 그러자 그들이 돌을 집어 그분을 향해 던지려고 했다. 그러나 예수께서는 몸을 숨기시고 성전 뜰을 떠나 나가셨다.
ko.R: 그러자 그들은 돌을 집어 들고 예수께 던지려고 했다. 그러나 예수께서는 몸을 숨기시고 성전 뜰 밖으로 나가셨다.

pt.L: Então pegaram pedras para atirar {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}}; mas Jesus se escondeu e saiu do templo.
pt.B: Diante disso, pegaram pedras para atirar {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}}, mas Jesus se escondeu e saiu do pátio do templo.
pt.R: Então eles pegaram pedras para atirar {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}}. Mas Jesus se escondeu e saiu da área do templo.

decisions.choice: picking up stones: to put him to death for blasphemy
decisions.reason: Stoning was the law's penalty for blasphemy (Leviticus 24:16). They act at once, without a trial, as they will try to do again in 10:31-33. It shows how they understood "I am" in verse 58.

decisions.choice: hid himself: a passive form with a reflexive sense
alternatives: was hidden, by God or by the crowd
decisions.reason: The form is passive, but verbs like this often have the sense of doing something to oneself, and John uses the same form in 12:36, "he went away and hid himself from them". John does not say how he escaped. His hour had not yet come (7:30; 8:20). A footnote gives "was hidden".

decisions.choice: ends with "went out of the temple" (SBLGNT)
alternatives: many later manuscripts add "going through the middle of them, and so he passed by"
decisions.reason: The longer ending is not in the older manuscripts. Its first part resembles Luke 4:30, where Jesus passes through the middle of a hostile crowd, and its last words lead into 9:1, where Jesus is "passing by". A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: temple courts (B); temple area (R)
decisions.reason: The word is the whole temple area, not the sanctuary (see the book's terms).

decisions.choice: At this (B); Then (R)
decisions.reason: The connecting word shows that they acted because of what he had just said.

decisions.choice: los atrios del templo (B); el patio del templo (R)
decisions.reason: The 2:14 choice for the whole temple area.

decisions.choice: Jésus se cacha (no span on the reflexive "se")
decisions.reason: English "hid himself" carries the deity_pronoun setting on "himself". French says it with the reflexive verb "se cacher", and a reflexive "se" is not capitalised even where divine pronouns are, so there is no span; adding "lui-même" would stress the subject in a way the Greek does not (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: o pátio do templo (B); a área do templo (R)
